game_over_ship: Your ship has been wrecked by misfortune at sea.
game_over_morale: Your crew has lost all spirit and deserted you.
mutiny_confrontation: The crew has had enough. Morale is gone, and the mood on deck has turned from despair to something more dangerous. Boots on the deck above — too many, moving with purpose. They are not asking permission anymore.
mutiny_choice_stand_firm: Stand your ground — remind them who commands this ship.
mutiny_choice_appeal: Try to calm them — appeal to reason and promise fair treatment.
mutiny_outcome_talked_down: Something in your voice — or your nerve — reaches them. The ringleaders hesitate, then back down. It is not forgiveness, but it is enough. The crew returns to their posts, watching you differently now.
mutiny_outcome_concessions: You cannot fully regain control. To keep the ship from open violence, you are forced to hand over gold and cargo to quiet the loudest voices. The crew stands down — for now — but the debt is not forgotten.
mutiny_concessions_loss: You hand over {gold} gold and {cargo} units of cargo to buy peace.
mutiny_outcome_lost_ship: It is not enough. The crew seizes the ship. You are put over the side in a longboat with what you can carry, and watch your command sail on without you.
you_hesitate: You hesitate, and time slips by...
dialogue_denied_entry: You are turned away from the port. The deputy has made his decision.
dialogue_higher_fees: An additional fee of {fee} gold is demanded before you may proceed.
dialogue_cant_pay_fee: You cannot meet the additional fee. The official's patience is exhausted.
status_faction_note: Use [F] at port for full faction standing
slave_market_none: You have no enslaved persons aboard.
slave_market_free_one: Free one (costs {cost} gold at local rate)
slave_market_freed: {name} is freed. They walk off the ship without looking back.
slave_market_freed_all: All {count} are freed. The hold is empty.
slave_market_baraka_approves: Baraka watches this. He says nothing. But his bearing changes.
slave_market_purchased: You have purchased {count} enslaved person(s) for {cost} gold.
prisoner_take: Take as prisoners (ransom at next port)
prisoner_released_bonus: You release the captives. Your crew notes it.
homeport_locked: You have no reason to return yet. There is more to learn in these waters.
voyage_monsoon_blocked_warning: ⚠ The season is against this crossing — {origin} to {dest}.
voyage_no_route_error: The pilot has no chart for this crossing: {error}.
access_warning_market: The market is closed. Return at dawn.
access_warning_harbor_master: The harbor master's office is dark. Come back in the morning.
access_warning_ruler_audience: The palace is not receiving visitors at this hour.
access_warning_recruitment: The docks are quiet. Recruits will be here in the morning.
access_warning_quest_board: Officials are not available until morning.
access_warning_ship_repair: The shipwrights are not working at this hour.
ending_crew_lost: With no one left to work the sails, your voyage ends here. The sea keeps what it takes.
ending_companions_lost: {A} and {B} are gone. Without them you are a man with a ship and no reason to sail it. You sell her at the next port and are never heard from again.
ending_lost_at_sea: You sailed out of sight of land toward {dest}. Somewhere past the edge of the charts, the water ran out before the voyage did. No one ever learned what became of you.
warn_uncharted_portuguese: Captain, no. Nobody crosses that in one leg. We'd lose sight of land, then lose the ship. Take us to {hop} first.
warn_provisions_portuguese: That run needs {need} in stores and we carry {have}. I'll sail it if you order it, but we'll be burying men off the stern.
warn_uncharted_ottoman: Are you mad? No pilot from Aden to Zanzibar would take that crossing straight. We go by {hop}, God willing, or we go to the bottom.
warn_provisions_ottoman: The crossing wants {need} in stores. We hold {have}. Even Ibn Majid's charts cannot feed a hungry crew.
warn_uncharted_chinese: Aiya. Open water that long? The sea doesn't care what you paid for this junk. We stop at {hop}, burn incense, then talk.
warn_provisions_chinese: This run eats {need} in stores. We have {have}. Mazu can calm the sea. She can't fill the rice barrels.
voyage_read_portuguese: You read the psalms from your Book of Hours. Most of the men can't follow the Latin. They bow their heads anyway.
voyage_read_ottoman: You recite from the Qur'an as the sun goes down. The men answer the verses they know, and the deck goes quiet in a way it hasn't for days.
voyage_read_chinese_full: You read from the Diamond Sutra. The Buddhists among the crew murmur along. Wei Chongde listens with the patience of a Confucian being polite.
voyage_read_chinese_short: You read from the Diamond Sutra. The Buddhists among the crew murmur along.
voyage_story_result: {name} tells a long story about a sailor who married a sea-woman and lost her over a broken promise. The crew argues about the ending until dark.
voyage_fish_success: {name} hauls a fat fish over the rail to a cheer from the deck.
voyage_fish_failure: The lines come up empty. The sea keeps its own counsel today.
voyage_hunt_success: {name} comes back out of the trees with a deer and a story about the one that got away.
voyage_hunt_failure: The hunting party comes back muddy, bitten, and empty-handed.
effect_lose_hostage: {hostage} is no longer with your crew.
shore_leave_morale: Shore leave. The crew comes back from town louder than they left. (+12 morale)
crew_bonus_paid: You pay out a bonus on deck. The crew counts it twice and decides you're not so bad. (+{n} morale)
voyage_flavor_1: A flying fish lands on deck. Three men fight over who gets to eat it.
voyage_flavor_2: The water barrels are going green. The cook swears it's still fine.
voyage_flavor_3: Someone carved a woman's name into the mast. Nobody will admit to it.
voyage_flavor_4: For two days the sea has been the color of oil. The old hands don't like it.
voyage_flavor_5: A dead calm at noon. The sails hang like laundry.
voyage_flavor_6: Rats in the biscuit again. The ship's cat has given up.
voyage_flavor_7: At night the wake glows green. The men argue over whether it's spirits.
voyage_flavor_8: A sailor's tooth comes out in his bread. He keeps it for luck.
voyage_blocked_estimate: Attempting it now would take an estimated {days} day(s), sailing against the monsoon.
voyage_option_wait: Wait in port for the season to turn
warn_monsoon_portuguese: Against the monsoon, on open water? We'll be tacking for weeks, and the storms out there don't care whose flag we fly.
warn_monsoon_ottoman: Every pilot from Hormuz to Kilwa waits for this wind. Only fools and the desperate sail against it. Which are we today?
warn_monsoon_chinese: Wrong season for deep water. The junk can do it. The question is whether we want to arrive.
departure_favorable: The monsoon fills your sails from astern. The crew is singing by noon.
departure_transition: The winds can't make up their minds. Neither can the sea.
departure_against_coastal: You work up the coast against the monsoon, riding the land breeze at dawn and the sea breeze at dusk, anchoring when both fail.
departure_against_open_ocean: You turn into the teeth of the monsoon, out where there is no coast to shelter under.
role_ship_portuguese: Ship: a square-rigged nau. Hold: 50. Fast on open water, slow against the wind.
role_ship_ottoman: Ship: a lateen-rigged dhow. Hold: 40. Small, but she sails closest to the wind.
role_ship_chinese: Ship: an ocean junk. Hold: 60. The biggest hold, quick along the coast, slow on open water.
